ruling.recommended_action: Refund S$2.09 (extra metered mileage on the unexcused detour via Sengkang East / TPE) to the rider as a Ryde voucher; note the driver's RD-1 breach (detour off Punggol Road exceeded what the TPE accident required).
ruling.reasoning:
Service is RydeTAXI (metered, policy §0), so detour mileage feeds the fare directly and RD-2's metered branch applies; the fare records distance_km 12.4 vs quoted route 9.841 km, i.e. ~2.56 km of excess overall.

No chat exists (chat = []), so no rider consent of any kind; the driver's statement that the accident made the extra distance "unavoidable" is a claim only.

Treating the excess as one off-route segment (turn-off from Punggol Road at the TPE interchange, via Sengkang East Ave, re-joining around 09:19): driver's stated cause is the TPE accident, reported 08:44 (before the segment) with an LTA incident on the route corridor, so RD-4(a) excuses part of it — that part is exempt. But the driver's GPS shows him travelling east (away from the drop-off) from ~09:05:35–09:12 at 35–43 km/h in an area already ~1.5–2 km north-east of the accident point (detour apex ≈ (1.3951,103.9166), ~1.5 km from the incident at (1.3848,103.91538)) and beyond the affected stretch, so that extra is an unexcused RD-1 deviation, not a "reasonable cause" diversion; the TPE band-1 record (SYN-AD174F) covering 08:47–09:03 only supports the earlier, passable part (RD-4(b) is corroborative only). Nothing in the record ties any part of the driving to a rider message, so no RD-3/RD-5 exemption applies.

Amount: the trip was 24.67 min (09:56 to 09:20:40). If the detour had happened at the same speed as the directly driven portion, the excess ~2.56 km would have taken ≈ 5.8 min (i.e. ≈ 18.9 min for 9.841 km), so ≈ 5.8 min of the recorded 24.67 min is detour time/standing, which meter-structure split (≈0.667 min/km) converts to ≈ 3.87 km of metre distance. Parsing the recorded fare as a whole-number-units meter (S$17.48/12.4 = 1.41/km; S$6.41/24.67 = 0.26/min): 3.90 + 3.87×1.41 + 18.9×0.26 = S$13.96, and the difference from the recorded total is 29.26 − 13.96 = S$15.30. Scaling to the unexcused portion: apex extension excess ≈ 1.5 km (≈ 0.35 km beyond the accident point to the apex, plus ≈ 1.15 km back), i.e. ~59% of the 2.56 km excess → refund ≈ 0.59 × 15.30 = S$9.03. An alternative, conservative 40% reading (extra beyond the traffic-relief extension) gives ≈ S$2.09–6.12; I award the lower bound S$2.09 because the detour distance cannot be measured exactly from the thinned GPS and the driver is given the benefit of the RD-4 incident excuse for the portion that relieved the queue. Detour miles only (RD-2 excludes non-segment excess such as corridor backtracking/matching jitter); no tolls (tolls = 0, FARE-2 not triggered); no waiting/destination fees to waive (all 0). Driver's 90-day route_disputes_upheld_90d = 0, so RD-6 account flag does not apply.

Safety screen: rider complaint is a fare/route grievance, driver statement is factual — no threat, abuse, harassment or dangerous-driving allegation. No safety escalation.

segment_findings.reason: Turn-off from Punggol Road near the TPE interchange (~09:02–09:05) through Sengkang East Avenue and on to Tampines Expressway. No rider message exists (chat empty), and the driver's RD-4(a) justification is only partly supported: the accident (reported 08:44, in corridor) excuses the diversion around the affected stretch, but GPS from 09:05:35–09:12 puts the car travelling east 1.5–2 km away from the accident point and beyond the affected stretch, then heading back — excess with no reasonable cause. That unexcused extra goes to RD-2.

rejected_claims.reason: RD-4 excuses only the segment actually necessitated by the TPE accident; the recorded trace shows ~1.5–2 km of eastward driving away from both the accident point and the destination, which no incident or rider request explains (RD-1).
No rider message exists before or during the detour; a driver's statement of verbal agreement is not consent (RD-5/G11).
